stem: In 6473, the digit 4 stands for ________.
working: 6473 → 6 thousands, 4 hundreds, 7 tens, 3 ones. The 4 is in the hundreds place, so it stands for 400.

distractors.1: that is the digit, not its value

stem: Which of the following is the simplest form of 8/12?
working: 8 and 12 can both be cut by 4: 8 ÷ 4 = 2, 12 ÷ 4 = 3 → 2/3.

distractors.1: 4/6 is equivalent but can still be cut by 2

stem: Express 2 ℓ 350 ml in millilitres.
Which of the following shows 4.05 p.m. in the 24-hour clock?
working: Afternoon → add 12 to the hour: 4 + 12 = 16. Minutes stay the same → 16 05.
Watch out: p.m. hours get +12; the minutes never change.

stem: Name the obtuse angle in the figure.
working: An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle (bigger than the corner of a page). Only ∠b opens wider than a square corner; ∠a, ∠c and ∠d are all smaller than a right angle (acute).
Watch out: Test with the corner of a piece of paper: if the corner fits inside with room to spare, the angle is obtuse.

distractors.1: ∠a is just under a right angle — acute

stem:
What is the missing number in the number pattern?

4160, 4260, 4210, 4310, ________, 4360, 4310
working: The steps alternate: +100, −50, +100, −50, …
Watch out: Write the step between every pair of numbers before guessing.

distractors.3: added 50 — that is the next term

stem: Marcus has 245 football cards. He has 68 fewer cards than Kai. How many cards do they have altogether?
working: "68 fewer than Kai" → Kai has MORE. Kai = 245 + 68 = 313.
Altogether: 245 + 313 = 558.
Watch out: Circle the name after 'fewer than' — that person has more.

stem: A toy robot costs $36.45. Mrs Lee paid for it with a $50 note. How much change did she receive?

distractors.2: forgot to rename when subtracting cents

stem: The bar graph shows the number of cups of bubble tea sold at a stall from Monday to Thursday. How many more cups were sold on Wednesday than on Tuesday?
working: Each small line is 2 cups. Wednesday = 34, Tuesday = 18.
Watch out: Count the small gridlines; do not round to the nearest labelled line.

stem: The figure is made up of straight lines meeting at right angles. What is the perimeter of the figure?
working: The unlabelled inside edge = 12 − 6 = 6 cm.
Watch out: Label every edge before you add. An L-shape has six edges, not four.

distractors.1: left out the 6 cm inside edge

stem: Write **eight thousand and seven** in numerals.
working: 8 thousands, 0 hundreds, 0 tens, 7 ones → 8007.
Common error: Writing 807 or 8070 — use a place-value chart with four boxes.

stem: Multiply 248 by 7.
working: Common error: Forgetting to add the carried number.

stem: What is the fraction represented by A on the number line?
working: Count the gaps from 0 to 1: 9 equal parts. A is at the 5th mark → 5/9.
Common error: Counting the marks instead of the gaps (gives 5/8 or 5/10).

stem: A skipping rope is 3 m 40 cm long. Express its length in centimetres.
working: Common error: Writing 3040 cm (treating 40 as 040) or 304 cm.

stem: Marcus had $40. He bought a comic book for $17.35. How much money had he left?
working: Common error: Getting $23.65 by subtracting 35 cents from a whole dollar without renaming.

stem: In the grid, which line is perpendicular to line PQ?
working: PQ goes 1 across, 1 down for every square. A perpendicular line swaps the steps and turns one around: 1 across, 1 up. That is RS.
VW is parallel to PQ (same steps). TU goes 2 across, 1 down — neither.
Common error: Choosing VW — parallel lines look 'matching', perpendicular lines make a corner.
marking: A2 for RS; A1 for VW with a note about parallel (shows the right idea, wrong relationship)

stem: A baker packed 925 cookies into bags of 8. After filling as many bags as he could, how many cookies were left over?
working: 5 cookies were left over.
Common error: Answering 115 (the number of bags) when the question asks for the leftover.

stem: Find the value of 5/6 − 1/3. Give your answer in its simplest form.
working: 1/3 = 2/6 (×2 top and bottom).
Common error: Leaving 3/6; or subtracting tops and bottoms separately (4/3).
marking: M1 for 2/6, A1 for 1/2 (3/6 gets M1 only)

stem: Marcus started his piano practice at 16 45 and finished at 18 10. How long did he practise? Give your answer in hours and minutes.
working: 15 min + 1 h + 10 min = 1 h 25 min.
Common error: 18 10 − 16 45 as a subtraction in base 10 (gives 1 h 65 min or 2 h 35 min).
marking: M1 for a correct time line / jumps, A1 for 1 h 25 min

stem: The figures are not drawn to scale. Find the area of Figure P and the area of Figure Q. Then state which figure has the larger perimeter.
answer: Area P = 36 cm², Area Q = 36 cm²; Figure Q has the larger perimeter
working: Area P = 6 × 6 = 36 cm². Area Q = 3 × 12 = 36 cm². Same area!
Perimeter P = 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24 cm. Perimeter Q = 3 + 12 + 3 + 12 = 30 cm. Q is larger.
Common error: Assuming same area means same perimeter.
marking: A1 for both areas with cm², A1 for Q (with perimeters shown)

stem:
A hawker sold 1250 plates of chicken rice over three days. He sold 468 plates on Friday and 395 plates on Saturday.

(a) How many plates did he sell on Friday and Saturday altogether?
working: He sold 863 plates on Friday and Saturday altogether.

stem:
A hawker sold 1250 plates of chicken rice over three days. He sold 468 plates on Friday and 395 plates on Saturday.

(b) How many plates did he sell on Sunday?
working: He sold 387 plates on Sunday.
Common error: Subtracting only one day: 1250 − 468.
marking: M1 for 1250 − 863 (follow-through from (a) allowed), A1 for 387

stem:
Sticker packs are sold at the prices shown.

(a) Mei bought 4 packs, one at a time. How much did she pay?

Sticker packs are sold at the prices shown.

(b) Raj wanted 13 packs. What is the least amount of money he could pay?
working: 5 packs for $12 is cheaper than 5 × $3 = $15, so buy as many groups of 5 as possible.
$12 + $12 = $24 (two groups of 5)
3 × $3 = $9 (three single packs)
The least amount he could pay is $33.
Common error: Buying 3 groups of 5 (15 packs, $36) — more packs than he wanted and more money; or 13 × $3 = $39.
marking: M1 for grouping 13 = 5 + 5 + 3, M1 for $24 and $9, A1 for $33

stem:
A football match started at 2.40 p.m. The first half lasted 45 minutes. Then there was a 15-minute break before the second half started.
(Draw a time line to show your working.)

(a) At what time did the second half start?
working: 2.40 p.m. + 45 min → 3.25 p.m. (20 min to 3.00, then 25 more)
The second half started at 3.40 p.m.
marking: M1 for 3.25 p.m., A1 for 3.40 p.m.

stem:
A football match started at 2.40 p.m. The first half lasted 45 minutes. Then there was a 15-minute break before the second half started.
(Draw a time line to show your working.)

(b) Marcus took 50 minutes to travel to the stadium. He arrived 20 minutes before the match started. At what time did he leave home?
working: Arrived: 2.40 p.m. − 20 min = 2.20 p.m.
Left home: 2.20 p.m. − 50 min = 1.30 p.m. (20 min back to 2.00, then 30 more)
He left home at 1.30 p.m.
Common error: Adding the 50 and 20 minutes to 2.40 instead of going backwards.
marking: M1 for 2.20 p.m., A1 for 1.30 p.m.

stem:
The bar graph shows the number of goals scored by Class 3A and Class 3B in each round of a football tournament.

(a) In which round did Class 3B score 6 more goals than Class 3A?

The bar graph shows the number of goals scored by Class 3A and Class 3B in each round of a football tournament.

(b) How many goals did Class 3A score altogether?

The bar graph shows the number of goals scored by Class 3A and Class 3B in each round of a football tournament.

(c) Each goal earns 3 points. How many more points did Class 3B earn than Class 3A over the four rounds?
working: Class 3B: 8 + 5 + 10 + 9 = 32 goals
32 − 30 = 2 more goals
2 × 3 = 6 more points
Class 3B earned 6 more points.
Common error: Answering 2 (goals, not points).
marking: M1 for 32 (or 96 and 90 points), A1 for 6

stem:
Marcus, Kai and Mia collected 162 seashells altogether. Kai collected 3 times as many seashells as Marcus. Mia collected 12 more seashells than Marcus.

(a) If Mia had collected 12 fewer seashells, how many seashells would the three children have collected altogether?

Marcus, Kai and Mia collected 162 seashells altogether. Kai collected 3 times as many seashells as Marcus. Mia collected 12 more seashells than Marcus.

(b) How many seashells did Kai collect?
working: Draw the model: Marcus 1 unit, Kai 3 units, Mia 1 unit + 12.
Kai collected 90 seashells.
Common error: Dividing 162 by 5; or answering 30 (Marcus) instead of Kai.
marking: M1 for a correct model or 5 units = 150, M1 for 1 unit = 30, A1 for 90
